text:
incident-bot: ALERT severity=2 private-cluster=acme-edge region=eu-west-1 summary=autoscaler failed to provision GPUs; queue_length=3120; symptom=pods_pending > 15m; reason='quota_or_maxnodes_reached' :rotating_light:

alice.nguyen: I'm paged, looking. Can someone drop the autoscaler logs and nodepool status?

ben.kapoor: digging in. kube events show a bunch of FailedCreatePodSandBox and provider errors. suspect cloud quota hit or nodepool hit maxNodes. will pull cloud API call logs.

sara.dominguez: customer impact: ACME Edge (private) is hitting 5% error rate for inference requests and queued requests are growing. customer has SLOs for 99.9 latency. paging sales CSM after we stabilize.

infra-bot: autoscaler logs (last 15m):
```
ERROR autoscaler: scale_up: desired=24 current=24 max=24 reason=Reached maxNodes for nodepool gpu-pool-edge
WARN provider: quotaExceeded: Request for GPUs denied: "INSUFFICIENT_PROJECT_QUOTA"
```

jonah: confirmed nodepool already at maxNodes=24 in cluster config. Cloud API shows quota limit for NVIDIA_A100=0 additional. Provisioning attempts are stuck in creating state for ~12m.

alice.nguyen: Action list: (1) enable cross-tenant fallback routing to hosted Redwood pool for non-sensitive requests, (2) attempt manual create of a new nodepool with different instance type + smaller GPU count, (3) open support case with cloud provider to raise quota, (4) notify customer leads. I'm going to hand off after 30m if not resolved.

ben.kapoor: trying manual nodepool create with spot+passthrough type g4dn.xlarge as temp. command: 
```
# creating temp nodepool
cloudctl nodepool create --cluster acme-edge --name temp-gpu-burst --machine-type g4dn.xlarge --gpu 1 --count 10
```

infra-bot: cloud API response: 202 Accepted -> resource temp-gpu-burst in provisioning state; but subsequent events show provisioning stuck: "ResourceCreationTimeout" with provider error code 4201.

alice.nguyen: rolling fallback: enabling route policy for acme-edge to send low-priority traffic to hosted-redwood eu-west-1-burst. This will reduce private cluster queue while preserving private-only workloads. toggling now.

sara.dominguez: pinging CSM and ops contact at ACME. Messaging: "We've detected autoscaler failures; temporarily routing non-sensitive inference traffic to hosted pool to keep your product online. We'll follow up with a timeline once provider quota confirmed."

support-bot: ticket created: CLOUD-78932 (quota request submitted). ETA from cloud provider: initial response 2-4 hours.

jonah: manual nodepool still not ready; provisioning logs show network attach timeout to VPC ENI. Likely cloud provider resource scarcity in that AZ. Trying creation in alternate AZ (eu-west-1b -> eu-west-1c).

ben.kapoor: created temp-gpu-burst-2 in eu-west-1c; initial success. kube nodes joined cluster: 8/10 ready, kubelet warnings for device plugin but GPU drivers loaded.

alice.nguyen: good. Starting gradual drain of pending pods onto temp-gpu-burst-2. monitoring queue.

infra-bot: queue length trend: 3120 -> 2100 -> 900 -> 120 over 18 minutes after fallback and temp nodepool.

sara.dominguez: customer update sent. ACME ops replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted. Are logs retained for audit?" I told them we'll share postmortem and kube events.

alice.nguyen: current status: partial mitigation in place (hosted fallback + temp nodepool). Root cause still: autoscaler hit configured maxNodes and cloud provider quota constraints + AZ-specific provisioning failures.

oncall-rotation: handing off to ben for next 2h. ben, you'll own until cleared or further handoff.

ben.kapoor: taking over. next steps: (A) keep temp nodepool until cloud quota resolved, (B) reduce autoscaler sensitivity to prevent cascade in future, (C) update runbook to try alt-AZ nodepool creation automatically if provisioning in primary AZ fails for >60s, (D) schedule quota request escalation with cloud rep.

alice.nguyen: thanks. I'll start the incident doc and capture timelines. Reminder: do not route PII / private-data requests to hosted pool — routing policy explicitly excludes requests with header X-tenant-sensitive=true.

infra-bot: scheduled cleanup job created: temp-gpu-burst-2 -> TTL 8 hours unless flagged keep.

support-bot: created customer incident ACME-INC-2026-03-14 and attached CLOUD-78932.

jonah: note for follow-up: autoscaler metrics show burst of requests ~09:12 UTC correlated with customer deployment. Consider autoscale threshold tuning and warm pool for biggest private clusters.

ben.kapoor: doing a quick patch to the cluster autoscaler config to bump maxNodes for gpu-pool-edge from 24 -> 36 while we await quota (this will allow provider errors to surface quicker if quota denied). Patching now:
```
kubectl patch cm cluster-autoscaler-config -n kube-system --patch '{"data":{"gpu-pool-edge.maxNodes":"36"}}'
```

infra-bot: patch applied. Note: increase will not overcome cloud quota; it prevents autoscaler from hitting a software cap.

alice.nguyen: timeline note: 09:09 incident bot alert -> 09:20 fallback routing -> 09:34 temp nodepool ready -> 09:52 queue drained to normal.

sara.dominguez: customer ops confirmed service restored. CSM asked for postmortem by EOD.

ben.kapoor: next-day action items I already filed: escalate quota with cloud rep (CLOUD-78932), add auto-alt-az nodepool creation to runbook (RB-154), add warm pool recommendation for clusters >20k qps, and a short-term autoscaler config change template.

alice_nguyen: closing notes: no data exfiltration, no PII routed to hosted pool, customer impact window ~ 09:09-09:52 UTC. I'll convert this thread into an incident report skeleton.

oncall-rotation: resolved? if yes react with :white_check_mark: and we'll mark incident closed after postmortem doc.

ben.kapoor: :white_check_mark: closing oncall.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: root_cause=quota_and_az_provisioning; mitigations=hosted_fallback,temp_nodepool,autoscaler_config_patch; duration_minutes=43; followups=RB-154,CLOUD-78932
